 370	//
 371	// Root-relative inside the project. Root-relative one level up too — a file
 372	// beside the project directory, or one inside a sibling of it — because
 373	// ../spec.md and ../sibling-repo/include/api.h say something an absolute path
 374	// does not: that the file sits next to the work. Absolute beyond that.
 375	//
 376	// The relative-inside, absolute-outside half is not a new rule; toProjectPaths
 377	// has written the resume file that way all along, on the grounds that a
 378	// reference reached outside the project has no project-relative form worth
 379	// keeping. The one-level exception is display's own, and storage deliberately
 380	// does not take it: a stored ../sibling breaks the moment the project moves,
 381	// while a name on screen only has to be right now. Two jobs, two rules, and the
 382	// divergence is in a file nobody reads.
 383	//
 384	// What it replaces named an out-of-tree pin by counting back to it, so
 385	// /usr/include/foo.h from a project three levels down read as
 386	// ../../../usr/include/foo.h — correct, and reading as though the file were
 387	// part of the project when the whole point of /read-only is that it is not.
 388	//

 390	// model call the file the same thing. That works because Workspace.contain
 391	// admits an absolute path for a pinned file, the same exemption unsafePath

 397	// displayName is DisplayPath for a caller that already holds a resolved
 398	// absolute path, skipping the re-resolve. Everything that names a pinned file
 399	// goes through one of the two.
 400	func (c *Coder) displayName(abs string) string {
 401		rel := c.relFname(abs)
 402		up, rest := 0, rel
 403		for {
 404			if rest == ".." {
 405				up++
 406				rest = ""
 407				break
 408			}
 409			if !strings.HasPrefix(rest, "../") {
 410				break
 411			}
 412			up++
 413			rest = rest[len("../"):]
 414		}
 415		// rest == "" is the project's parent directory itself, which is not a file
 416		// anyone pins; it falls through to the absolute form rather than being
 417		// named "..".
 418		if up == 0 || (up == 1 && rest != "") {
 419			return rel
 420		}
 421		// Native separators, not ToSlash. A root-relative name is the tool-facing

 476	// confirmGrouped wraps c.Confirm with group-scoped auto-approve. If the user
 477	// answered "a" to a previous Confirm with the same Group, this one is approved
 478	// without prompting. The first "a" answer records the group and returns true.
 479	// req.GroupSession picks how long the record lasts — the session, or the turn.
 480	// Callers that don't need grouping — confirmMoreSteps, checkTokens — call
 481	// c.Confirm.Confirm directly.
 482	//
 483	// Both maps are read on every call regardless of scope. A group is only ever
 484	// written to one of them, so this cannot widen a grant; what it does is keep a
 485	// session grant honored by a request that forgot to set GroupSession.
 486	func (c *Coder) confirmGrouped(req ConfirmRequest) bool {
 487		if req.Group != "" && (c.turnAutoApprove[req.Group] || c.sessionAutoApprove[req.Group]) {
 488			return true
 489		}
 490		res := c.Confirm.Confirm(req)
 491		if res.Always && req.Group != "" {
 492			if req.GroupSession {
 493				c.sessionAutoApprove[req.Group] = true
 494			} else {
 495				c.turnAutoApprove[req.Group] = true
 496			}
 497		}
 498		return res.Yes || res.Always

 510	// runOne is the turn loop. It keeps sending while the model has something to
 511	// react to — a tool result it hasn't seen (OutcomeContinue) or a mistake to fix
 512	// (OutcomeReflect) — and stops when the model has nothing left to say, the
 513	// human interrupts, or a budget is spent. The turn boundary is still the
 514	// human's: nothing here starts new work of its own.
 515	func (c *Coder) runOne(ctx context.Context, userMessage string) {
 516		c.initBeforeMessage()
 517		c.turnHistory = ""
 518	
 519		if userMessage == "" {
 520			return
 521		}
 522		message := userMessage
 523	
 524		// Committing and rotating settled history are both turn-end concerns.
 525		// Mid-loop the tool results must stay in cur, and summarizing them away
 526		// between steps would compact the very results the next send reacts to;
 527		// committing mid-loop would spend one commit per send on fragments of one
 528		// change. A defer covers every exit — budget declined, reflection cap,
 529		// interrupted, or done. An interrupted turn's edits are real, so they are
 530		// committed too.
 531		defer func() {
 532			c.settleEdits("")
 533			c.endTurnHistory()
 534			// Last, so the accounting closes the turn: the commit line above it, and
 535			// nothing under it. This is what the per-send reorder was reaching for,
 536			// now at the scope where a reader actually wants the number. Once per
 537			// turn even when the turn was steered, because a steered turn is still
 538			// one turn's spend.
 539			c.flushTurnUsage()
 540		}()
 541	
 542		// Outcome-driven so a re-send that carries no message text — both a tool
 543		// reflection and a tool continuation re-enter on the appended tool results
 544		// — keeps the loop going.
 545		for {
 546			outcome, reflection := c.sendSteerable(ctx, message)
 547			// After the send, not during it: sendMessage does its interrupt
 548			// handling before returning, and that handling can retract messages.
 549			c.recordNewMessages()
 550			c.lastSendOutcome = outcome
 551	
 552			switch outcome {
 553			case OutcomeReflect:
 554				if c.numReflections >= c.MaxErrorReflections {
 555					c.Out.Warningf("Only %d reflections allowed, stopping.", c.MaxErrorReflections)
 556					return
 557				}
 558				c.numReflections++
 559				message = reflection
 560	
 561			case OutcomeContinue:
 562				c.numSteps++
 563				if c.numSteps >= c.MaxSteps && !c.confirmMoreSteps() {
 564					return
 565				}
 566				message = "" // the tool results are the message
 567	
 568			case OutcomeSuccess:
 569				// The model has nothing more to call, so it believes it is done.
 570				// That is the moment to check, if the project asked us to.
 571				report, ok := c.runAutoCheck(ctx)
 572				if !ok {
 573					return
 574				}
 575				message = report
 576	
 577			case OutcomeInterrupted:
 578				next, keepGoing := c.afterInterrupt()
 579				if !keepGoing {
 580					return
 581				}
 582				c.accumulateInterrupt(next)
 583				message = next
 584	
 585			case OutcomeLooping:
 586				next, keepGoing := c.afterLoop()
 587				if !keepGoing {
 588					return
 589				}
 590				c.accumulateInterrupt(next)
 591				message = next
 592	
 593			default:
 594				return
 595			}
 596		}
 597	}

 599	// accumulateInterrupt saves the content of a send that was stopped before the
 600	// next send resets it, so the transcript can show the full arc of a steered
 601	// turn: what the model was saying, the steer, and the final answer.
 602	//
 603	// The steer is included when the user typed a custom correction rather than
 604	// choosing "Continue" (which carries no user text). A blockquote prefix makes
 605	// the authorship unambiguous in the markdown transcript.
 606	func (c *Coder) accumulateInterrupt(steer string) {
 607		if c.partialResponseContent != "" {
 608			c.turnHistory += c.partialResponseContent + "\n\n"
 609		}
 610		if steer != "" {
 611			c.turnHistory += "> " + strings.ReplaceAll(steer, "\n", "\n> ") + "\n\n"
 612		}
 613	}

 615	// sendSteerable runs one send under a context of its own, so that stopping the
 616	// send does not have to mean ending the turn.
 617	//
 618	// This is the whole of the change that makes steering possible. Ctrl-C used to
 619	// cancel the *turn's* context: everything downstream saw Canceled from then on,
 620	// and there was no way back into the loop even though the conversation itself
 621	// had survived intact. A child context per send moves the blast radius to the
 622	// one send, and the turn context stays live to make the next one.
 623	//
 624	// The tool calls of a send run inside it too — applyToolCalls takes this same
 625	// context — so Ctrl-C still kills a bash command that is running, which is the
 626	// property worth not losing.
 627	func (c *Coder) sendSteerable(ctx context.Context, message string) (SendOutcome, string) {
 628		sctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 629		c.sendMu.Lock()
 630		c.cancelSend = cancel
 631		c.sendMu.Unlock()
 632	
 633		defer func() {
 634			c.sendMu.Lock()
 635			c.cancelSend = nil
 636			c.sendMu.Unlock()
 637			cancel()
 638		}()
 639	
 640		return c.sendMessage(sctx, message)
 641	}

 643	// InterruptSend stops the send in flight without ending the turn.
 644	//
 645	// Called from the REPL's signal handler, which used to cancel the turn context
 646	// directly. A Ctrl-C between sends finds no send to cancel and does nothing,
 647	// which is correct: there is nothing in flight, and the prompt the user is
 648	// about to get asked is the interrupt they wanted.
 649	func (c *Coder) InterruptSend() {
 650		c.sendMu.Lock()
 651		cancel := c.cancelSend
 652		c.sendMu.Unlock()
 653		if cancel != nil {
 654			cancel()
 655		}
 656	}

 658	// settleEdits commits the turn's edits so far and records a snapshot to undo
 659	// them by.
 660	//
 661	// Factored out of the turn-end defer because an interruption is also a place
 662	// this belongs. The human stopped to look at something, which makes that point
 663	// a review boundary: `git show` gives exactly what the model did before it was
 664	// stopped, separately from what it did after the correction, and /undo steps
 665	// through the two halves one at a time. Anyone who wanted one commit has
 666	// /squash.
 667	//
 668	// What is *not* here is flushTurnUsage. The spend is a property of the turn,
 669	// not of each leg of it, so it stays in the defer and reports once.
 670	func (c *Coder) settleEdits(message string) {
 671		// Nothing written since the last settle, so there is nothing to settle.
 672		// Without this an interrupted-then-steered turn settles twice over the same
 673		// edits: the second commit finds the tree already matching HEAD and
 674		// announces "the turn left the files as they were", which is true of the
 675		// second attempt and false of the turn.
 676		//
 677		// turnSnap is the right signal rather than turnEditedFiles, which
 678		// accumulates across the whole turn because the history record at turn end
 679		// wants every file the turn touched. turnSnap is emptied by
 680		// pushTurnSnapshot and rebuilt by recordWrites, so it means precisely
 681		// "written since the last settle".
 682		if c.turnSnap.empty() {
 683			return
 684		}
 685		c.commitTurn(message)
 686		c.pushTurnSnapshot()
 687	}

 689	// afterInterrupt asks the human what a stopped turn should do next, and
 690	// reports the message to resume with and whether to resume at all.
 691	//
 692	// The choice is put through the Asker port, which is what ask_user_question
 693	// already uses to prompt in the middle of a turn — so this is a shape the
 694	// terminal handling has been driving all along rather than a new one. Free text
 695	// comes back as the raw line, which *is* the correction, so there is nothing to
 696	// parse. A nil Asker means no interactive terminal (script mode): stopping is
 697	// the only honest answer there, and it is what an interrupt has always done.
 698	//
 699	// The --yes flags deliberately do not answer this. They skip permission
 700	// prompts, and being asked what you meant by stopping is not a permission
 701	// prompt — the same line the port's own documentation draws for
 702	// ask_user_question.
 703	func (c *Coder) afterInterrupt() (message string, keepGoing bool) {
 704		if c.Asker == nil {
 705			return "", false
 706		}
 707		// The edits so far belong to the interrupt, whichever way this goes.
 708		c.settleEdits("")
 709	
 710		answer := c.Asker.Ask(AskRequest{
 711			Question: "You stopped the model. What now?",
 712			Options: []AskOption{
 713				{Label: "Continue", Description: "Carry on from where it was cut off"},
 714				{Label: "Stop", Description: "End the turn here"},
 715			},
 716		})
 717		if len(answer) == 0 {
 718			return "", false
 719		}
 720		switch answer[0] {
 721		case "Continue":
 722			// Say what the user decided, or the model is answering the wrong
 723			// question.
 724			//
 725			// noteInterrupt runs before this prompt, so all it can say is that the
 726			// reply was cut off. On its own that reads as a full stop, and the
 727			// model obliges: "No problem — I'll stop here. What would you like me
 728			// to do next?" It is not misreading anything. Asked afterwards what it
 729			// had been told, it quoted the cut-off note and said no continue choice
 730			// had reached it, which was exactly right.
 731			//
 732			// The rest of the wording closes the other failure mode. With a whole
 733			// partial reply above it and no instruction about what to do with it, a
 734			// model will also quite reasonably begin again from the top — which is
 735			// what an earlier live pass showed, and what was wrongly written up as
 736			// the cost of keeping the partial rather than as this bug.
 737			c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(
 738				"The user chose to continue. Pick up exactly where your reply above "+
 739					"stops and carry on from there — do not start over, do not repeat "+
 740					"or summarize what you already wrote, and do not ask what to do next."))
 741			// The notes are the message, so the next send re-enters on them rather
 742			// than appending an empty user turn to carry nothing.
 743			c.resumeInPlace = true
 744			return "", true
 745		case "Stop":
 746			return "", false
 747		default:
 748			// Anything else the user typed is the steer, and it goes in as their
 749			// own words in their own voice. They really did type it.
 750			return answer[0], true
 751		}
 752	}
 753	
 754	// afterLoop asks what to do about a reply the harness stopped for repeating
 755	// itself, and reports whether the turn should continue.
 756	//
 757	// Its own function rather than a branch of afterInterrupt, because both halves
 758	// differ. The question cannot say "you stopped the model" — the user did not —
 759	// and "Continue" cannot mean "pick up exactly where your reply stops", which
 760	// here is an instruction to resume the loop. What is offered instead is a
 761	// retry: the loop's note (send.go) tells the model to take a different
 762	// approach, and the most useful thing the user can do is type what that should
 763	// be, which the free-text steer already carries.
 764	func (c *Coder) afterLoop() (message string, keepGoing bool) {
 765		if c.Asker == nil {
 766			return "", false
 767		}
 768		// The edits so far belong to the stopped reply, whichever way this goes.
 769		c.settleEdits("")
 770	
 771		answer := c.Asker.Ask(AskRequest{
 772			Question: "The model was repeating itself and was stopped. What now?",
 773			Options: []AskOption{
 774				{Label: "Stop", Description: "End the turn here"},
 775				{Label: "Try again", Description: "Let it answer again, told not to repeat itself"},
 776			},
 777		})
 778		if len(answer) == 0 {
 779			return "", false
 780		}
 781		switch answer[0] {
 782		case "Stop":
 783			return "", false
 784		case "Try again":
 785			// The note noteLoop already appended is the whole message: it says what
 786			// was stopped and what to do instead, so the next send re-enters on it
 787			// rather than appending an empty user turn to carry nothing.
 788			c.resumeInPlace = true
 789			return "", true
 790		default:
 791			// Anything else the user typed is the steer, in their own voice.
 792			return answer[0], true
 793		}
 794	}

 796	// runAutoCheck runs the project's check_auto checks at the end of a turn that
 797	// edited files, and reports whether the turn should continue.
 798	//
 799	// It fires here rather than after each edit because a mid-turn state is
 800	// legitimately broken: edit one file, then its caller, and in between nothing
 801	// compiles. Checking there would spend budget on failures the model was already
 802	// about to fix. At turn end the model has declared itself finished, which is
 803	// exactly when an independent check is worth something — and the reason to make
 804	// it independent is that the model's judgement about *which* check mattered is
 805	// the part that fails. A run that passed the tests and never linted still
 806	// reports "the checks pass".
 807	//
 808	// The returned message is a user turn, not a tool result, which is a deliberate
 809	// exception to the rule that reflection is a tool error. There is no call to
 810	// answer here: the model did not ask for this, the harness is speaking
 811	// unprompted, and a user message is the honest shape for that.
 812	func (c *Coder) runAutoCheck(ctx context.Context) (message string, keepGoing bool) {
 813		// Nothing changed since the last run — either the turn edited nothing at
 814		// all, or the model replied to a failure without touching a file, which is
 815		// a considered answer ("that isn't mine") and not something to re-ask.
 816		if len(c.CheckAuto) == 0 || !c.editedSinceCheck {
 817			return "", false
 818		}
 819		c.editedSinceCheck = false
 820		if c.autoChecks >= maxAutoCheck {
 821			c.Out.Warningf("The automatic checks have run %d times without passing; stopping here.", maxAutoCheck)
 822			return "", false
 823		}
 824		c.autoChecks++
 825	
 826		c.Out.Toolf("Running the automatic checks.")
 827		transcript, passed := c.runChecks(ctx, c.CheckAuto)
 828		if passed {
 829			return "", false
 830		}
 831		// The wording matters, and live testing is what showed why. "did not pass
 832		// after your changes" reads as "you caused this", which puts the model
 833		// between this message and the standing instruction to leave unrelated code
 834		// alone. Observed: it declined to fix a pre-existing failure, was asked
 835		// again by the next round, and gave in — two rounds spent on an argument the
 836		// harness started. Saying plainly that reporting is an acceptable answer
 837		// settles it in one.
 838		return "The automatic checks ran after your changes and did not pass:\n\n" + transcript +
 839			"\nIf this is something you broke, fix it. If it was already failing and is unrelated to " +
 840			"what you changed, say so and stop — don't fix it unless the user asks.", true
 841	}

 843	// confirmMoreSteps is the budget checkpoint. A long turn is legitimate, but it
 844	// should not run away unnoticed, so the user is shown what it has done so far
 845	// and asked whether to keep going. Declining ends the turn normally, with the
 846	// work up to that point already applied and committed. Answering yes buys
 847	// another MaxSteps.
 848	func (c *Coder) confirmMoreSteps() bool {
 849		files := len(c.turnEditedFiles)
 850		noun := "files"
 851		if files == 1 {
 852			noun = "file"
 853		}
 854		c.Out.Printf("This turn has run %d steps and edited %d %s.", c.numSteps, files, noun)
 855		if c.costKnown {
 856			c.Out.Printf("Cost so far: $%s.", formatCost(c.messageCost))
 857		}
 858	
 859		res := c.Confirm.Confirm(ConfirmRequest{Prompt: "Keep going?", Grant: GrantSteps})
 860		if !res.Yes {
 861			c.Out.Printf("Stopping here. The work so far is applied; say what to do next.")
 862			return false
 863		}
 864		c.numSteps = 0
 865		c.autoChecks = 0
 866		c.editedSinceCheck = false
 867		return true
 868	}

 911		// it; repl/output.go's separateFromAnswer says why.
 912		if o.endReasoning() {
 913			fmt.Println()
 914			o.sep.Clear()
 915		}
 916		if delta != "" {
 917			o.wroteText = true
 918			o.streamed = true

 924	// StreamReasoning renders the model's thinking, plain.
 925	//
 926	// It used to be an empty function, so `strument -m … > transcript.txt` dropped
 927	// the whole reasoning trace without saying so, while the same session run
 928	// interactively showed it. Which mode you happened to use decided whether the
 929	// thinking existed — a decision nobody made, and one that cost several live
 930	// runs chasing a marker that could not appear. How much to show is now
 931	// reasoning_display's to answer, in both modes alike.
 932	func (o *StdOutput) StreamReasoning(delta string) {
 933		if o.think == nil {
 934			t := render.PlainThinking(os.Stdout, o.Thinking)
 935			// Pay the group separator at the opening marker: thinking opens lazily,
 936			// so a block that turns out to be empty never reaches Marker, and this
 937			// is the last point still above the "‹thinking›" the gap must precede.
 938			inner := t.Marker
 939			t.Marker = func(s string) {
 940				o.sep.Before(os.Stdout)
 941				o.streamed = true
 942				inner(s)
 943			}
 944			o.think = t
 945		}
 946		o.think.Write(render.Sanitize(delta))
 947	}

 949	// endReasoning closes an open thinking block and reports whether there was one.
 950	func (o *StdOutput) endReasoning() bool {
 951		if o.think == nil {
 952			return false
 953		}
 954		rendered := o.think.End()
 955		o.think = nil
 956		return rendered
 957	}

 959	func (o *StdOutput) StreamToolCall(index int, name, args string) {
 960		// Reasoning gave way to the calls it was about: no separator, since the
 961		// thinking heads this group. Clearing streamed by hand keeps the flush from
 962		// putting a blank directly above an outcome line printed by Toolf.
 963		if o.endReasoning() {
 964			o.streamed = false
 965		}
 966		if o.diffs == nil {
 967			// Break to a fresh line so the first diff header isn't glued to the
 968			// answer text (which need not end in a newline).
 969			if o.wroteText {
 970				fmt.Println()
 971				o.streamed = false // that blank separates; the flush need not repeat it
 972			}

 155				c.accumulateToolCall(ev.ToolCall)
 156				if ev.ToolCall != nil {
 157					c.Out.StreamToolCall(ev.ToolCall.Index, ev.ToolCall.Name, ev.ToolCall.Args)
 158				}
 159			case llm.EventFinish:
 160				finishReason = ev.FinishReason
 161			case llm.EventUsage:
 162				usage.add(ev.Usage)
 163			}
 164		}
 165		if finishReason == "length" {
 166			return resContinuation, nil
 167		}
 168		return resDone, nil
 169	}

 171	// retryBackoff carries the doubling delay for transient stream errors across a
 172	// send's retry loop.
 173	type retryBackoff struct{ delay time.Duration }
 174	
 175	// retry reports whether to retry a failed stream. A retryable error backs off —
 176	// doubling the delay (capped at retryTimeout) and sleeping — then returns true;
 177	// a non-retryable error, or one past the cap, reports the failure and returns
 178	// false. It takes Output and Clock rather than the Coder so the side-model
 179	// side calls (side.go) share it without owning one; sendMessage, RunAside, and
 180	// those side calls all retry identically.
 181	func (rb *retryBackoff) retry(out Output, clock Clock, streamErr error) bool {
 182		var se *llm.StreamError
 183		if !errors.As(streamErr, &se) || !se.Retryable() {
 184			out.Errorf("%v", streamErr)
 185			return false
 186		}
 187		rb.delay *= 2
 188		if rb.delay > retryTimeout {
 189			out.Errorf("%s", se.Error())
 190			return false
 191		}
 192		out.Warningf("%s", se.Error())
 193		out.Printf("Retrying in %.1f seconds...", rb.delay.Seconds())
 194		clock.Sleep(rb.delay)
 195		return true
 196	}

 198	// sendMessage is the phase machine. It returns the outcome and, for
 199	// OutcomeReflect, the next message to send.
 200	func (c *Coder) sendMessage(ctx context.Context, inp string) (SendOutcome, string) {
 201		// --- Setup ---
 202		// A resumed send re-enters on what is already in curMessages — tool
 203		// results, or an interrupted reply the user chose to continue — so it adds
 204		// no user turn; inp is unused on that path.
 205		appendedUser := false
 206		if c.resumeInPlace {
 207			c.resumeInPlace = false
 208		} else {
 209			c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.TextMessage("user", inp))
 210			appendedUser = true
 211		}
 212	
 213		chunks := c.formatMessages()
 214		messages := chunks.allMessages()
 215	
 216		if !c.checkTokens(messages) {
 217			if appendedUser {
 218				c.curMessages = c.curMessages[:len(c.curMessages)-1]
 219			}
 220			return OutcomeFailed, ""
 221		}
 222	
 223		// --- Stream ---
 224		c.multiResponseContent = "" // per-send reset (H1)
 225	
 226		usage := &sendUsage{estSent: c.countMessages(messages) + c.countTools()}
 227		defer c.finalizeUsage(usage)
 228	
 229		backoff := retryBackoff{delay: initialRetryDelay}
 230		continuations := 0
 231	
 232		// One detector per send, not per streamOnce: a continuation is the same
 233		// reply resumed, and a loop that spans the stitch is still a loop.
 234		loops := newLoopDetector(c.LoopDetection)
 235	
 236		// term is how the whole stream phase ended, as opposed to how one
 237		// streamOnce ended: retries and continuations loop without setting it.
 238		// streamOnce already classifies precisely, so the phase carries that
 239		// classification forward rather than re-encoding it into flags. Every path
 240		// out of the loop below assigns it before breaking.
 241		var term streamResult
 242	
 243		for {
 244			c.partialResponseContent = ""
 245			c.partialReasoningContent = ""
 246			c.partialToolCalls = nil
 247			c.toolCallIndex = map[int]int{}
 248	
 249			res, streamErr := c.streamOnce(ctx, c.buildRequest(messages), usage, loops)
 250	
 251			if res == resFailed {
 252				// A retryable error backs off and retries (the partial is discarded
 253				// at the loop top; accumulated multiResponseContent is untouched);
 254				// anything else is a hard failure.
 255				if backoff.retry(c.Out, c.Clock, streamErr) {
 256					continue
 257				}
 258				term = resFailed
 259				break
 260			}
 261	
 262			if res == resContinuation {
 263				if !c.PrefillSupported {
 264					term = resOutputExhausted
 265					break
 266				}
 267				continuations++
 268				if continuations > continuationCap {
 269					term = resOutputExhausted // cap hit
 270					break
 271				}
 272				// Stitch: accumulated + current partial becomes the prefill.
 273				c.multiResponseContent += c.partialResponseContent
 274				if n := len(messages); n > 0 && messages[n-1].Role == "assistant" {
 275					messages[n-1] = llm.TextMessage("assistant", c.multiResponseContent)
 276				} else {
 277					messages = append(messages, llm.TextMessage("assistant", c.multiResponseContent))
 278				}
 279				continue
 280			}
 281	
 282			term = res // resDone, resInterrupted, resLooping, resContextExhausted
 283			break
 284		}
 285		interrupted := term == resInterrupted
 286	
 287		// --- Finally (always runs) ---
 288		c.Out.FlushStream()
 289		answer := c.multiResponseContent + c.partialResponseContent
 290		answer = stripReasoning(answer, c.Model.ReasoningTag)
 291		c.partialResponseContent = answer
 292		c.multiResponseContent = ""
 293	
 294		// --- Post-stream dispatch ---
 295		c.finalizeUsage(usage)
 296	
 297		if answer != "" || len(c.partialToolCalls) > 0 {
 298			msg := llm.TextMessage("assistant", answer)
 299			if len(c.partialToolCalls) > 0 {
 300				msg.ToolCalls = c.partialToolCalls
 301			}
 302			c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, msg)
 303		}
 304	
 305		// dropUserTurn un-appends the user message this send added, so a send that
 306		// produced nothing doesn't poison the history. It is a no-op on a tool
 307		// continuation, which appended no user turn — truncating there would drop a
 308		// tool result and leave a tool_call unanswered, making the next request
 309		// malformed.
 310		dropUserTurn := func() {
 311			if appendedUser {
 312				c.curMessages = c.curMessages[:len(c.curMessages)-1]
 313			}
 314		}
 315	
 316		switch term {
 317		case resContextExhausted:
 318			// A system message, not an assistant one. The model did not say this —
 319			// the request never reached a reply — so putting it in the assistant's
 320			// voice fabricates a turn, and one in which the model appears to report
 321			// its own transport error. The note exists so the next request does not
 322			// end on a bare user turn with no answer, which is what the role check
 323			// below is for; whose voice carries it is a separate question, and the
 324			// harness's own is the honest one.
 325			if n := len(c.curMessages); n > 0 && c.curMessages[n-1].Role == "user" {
 326				c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages,
 327					llm.TextMessage(llm.RoleSystem, "The reply was cut off: the request exceeded the context limit."))
 328			}
 329			c.showExhaustedError()
 330			return OutcomeContextExhausted, ""
 331		case resOutputExhausted:
 332			// The large partial was kept above; no diagnostic (trailing message
 333			// is the assistant partial).
 334			return OutcomeOutputExhausted, ""
 335		case resFailed:
 336			if answer == "" {
 337				dropUserTurn()
 338			}
 339			return OutcomeFailed, ""
 340		case resLooping:
 341			// The user turn stays. Unlike an empty reply, this one produced
 342			// something — it produced too much of one thing — and the note below
 343			// only makes sense following the message it answers.
 344			c.warnLoop(loops.Found)
 345			c.noteLoop(loops.Found)
 346			return OutcomeLooping, ""
 347		}
 348	
 349		if !interrupted && answer == "" && len(c.partialToolCalls) == 0 {
 350			dropUserTurn()
 351			c.Out.Warningf("Empty response received from LLM. Check your provider account?")
 352			return OutcomeFailed, ""
 353		}
 354	
 355		if interrupted {
 356			c.noteInterrupt()
 357			return OutcomeInterrupted, ""
 358		}
 359	
 360		// Everything a turn does now arrives as tool calls, in every mode: ask mode
 361		// is the same dispatch with the mutating tools withheld. There is no longer
 362		// a second path that reads the answer text for edits, shell blocks, or file
 363		// mentions — those were the text formats' way of saying what a tool call
 364		// says directly.
 365		return c.applyToolCalls(ctx), ""
 366	}

 368	// noteInterrupt records that the human stopped the reply, in a shape the next
 369	// request can be built from.
 370	//
 371	// Two things it deliberately does not do, both of which it used to.
 372	//
 373	// It does not put words in the model's mouth. The old shape appended an
 374	// assistant turn saying "I see that you interrupted my previous reply", which
 375	// the model never said; the harness's own voice is the honest one, and the rest
 376	// of this file already says so about the context-exhausted note.
 377	//
 378	// It does not edit "^C KeyboardInterrupt" into the user's own message. Whatever
 379	// the human typed is what the human typed. assemble.go makes the same argument
 380	// about the system reminder, and this was the last place still doing it.
 381	//
 382	// The partial reply itself stays. It is real output the model produced, and
 383	// keeping it is what makes "continue as before" continue rather than restart.
 384	// Its *tool calls* do not stay — see dropPartialToolCalls.
 385	func (c *Coder) noteInterrupt() {
 386		c.dropPartialToolCalls()
 387		c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(
 388			"The user pressed Ctrl-C, so your reply above was cut off where it stops. "+
 389				"Anything you were part-way through saying was not finished, and any tool "+
 390				"call you had begun was not run — nothing it would have changed has changed."))
 391	}

 393	// warnLoop tells the user what the model was doing when it was stopped, in
 394	// every mode: script runs have no steer menu, and a run that stopped early is
 395	// the one thing a log must not be silent about.
 396	func (c *Coder) warnLoop(f *loopFinding) {
 397		if f == nil {
 398			c.Out.Warningf("The model's reply was repeating itself, so it was stopped.")
 399			return
 400		}
 401		c.Out.Warningf("The model's %s was repeating itself (%q %d times), so it was stopped.",
 402			f.Kind, f.Sample, f.Count)
 403	}

 405	// noteLoop records that the harness stopped a reply that was repeating itself.
 406	//
 407	// In the harness's own voice, for the same reason as noteInterrupt: nobody
 408	// pressed Ctrl-C, and saying the user did would be a fabrication about the one
 409	// participant whose actions the model cannot check.
 410	//
 411	// It quotes the repeating text back. A model given "you were repeating
 412	// yourself" and nothing else has to guess which part, and the guess is often
 413	// the whole reply; the sample makes the instruction actionable.
 414	func (c *Coder) noteLoop(f *loopFinding) {
 415		c.dropPartialToolCalls()
 416		where := "reply"
 417		if f != nil && f.Kind == loopReasoning {
 418			where = "reasoning"
 419		}
 420		note := "Strument stopped your " + where + " because it had begun repeating itself"
 421		if f != nil {
 422			note += fmt.Sprintf(" — %q appeared %d times", f.Sample, f.Count)
 423		}
 424		note += ". Nothing you were part-way through was finished, and any tool call " +
 425			"you had begun was not run. Do not continue that text or write it again: " +
 426			"take a different approach, and if you are stuck, say so plainly and stop."
 427		c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(note))
 428	}

 430	// noteToolInterrupt records a Ctrl-C that landed while a tool was running.
 431	//
 432	// Distinct from noteInterrupt, which describes a *stream* cut off mid-word and
 433	// says any tool call the model had begun was never run. Here the opposite is
 434	// true: the calls ran, their results are in the history, and one of them was
 435	// stopped part-way. Telling the model the other story would have it repeat work
 436	// that already happened, or distrust a result that is real.
 437	func (c *Coder) noteToolInterrupt() {
 438		c.partialToolCalls = nil
 439		c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(
 440			"The user pressed Ctrl-C while your tool calls were running. Their results "+
 441				"above are real as far as they got, and a command that was stopped says so "+
 442				"in its own output. Nothing after the interruption ran."))
 443	}

 445	// dropPartialToolCalls strips tool calls from the assistant message an
 446	// interrupted send just appended.
 447	//
 448	// Not tidiness — correctness. An unanswered tool_call makes the *next* request
 449	// malformed, and after an interrupt no result will ever answer one: the call is
 450	// either half-streamed and unparseable, or complete but never dispatched,
 451	// because the interrupt landed before applyToolCalls ran. Either way the model
 452	// must be told it did not happen, which the note above does, rather than shown
 453	// a call it may assume succeeded.
 454	//
 455	// The message's text survives. Only an assistant message can carry tool calls,
 456	// so this looks at one message and only when it is the last.
 457	func (c *Coder) dropPartialToolCalls() {
 458		c.partialToolCalls = nil
 459		n := len(c.curMessages)
 460		if n == 0 {
 461			return
 462		}
 463		last := &c.curMessages[n-1]
 464		if last.Role != llm.RoleAssistant || len(last.ToolCalls) == 0 {
 465			return
 466		}
 467		if last.Text() == "" {
 468			// Nothing but the abandoned calls: drop the whole turn rather than
 469			// leave an empty assistant message in the history.
 470			c.curMessages = c.curMessages[:n-1]
 471			return
 472		}
 473		last.ToolCalls = nil
 474	}

 476	// buildRequest translates state into an llm.Request.
 477	func (c *Coder) buildRequest(messages []llm.Message) llm.Request {
 478		req := llm.Request{
 479			Model:           c.Model.Slug,
 480			Messages:        messages,
 481			Temperature:     c.Model.Temperature,
 482			ReasoningEffort: c.Model.Reasoning,
 483			ExtraParams:     c.Model.RequestExtraParams(),
 484		}
 485		// Whatever tools this mode offers, offer them. The condition used to be
 486		// editFormat == "tool", which meant ask mode sent none at all — and made
 487		// toolDefs's own "ask" branch unreachable, so the code read as though ask
 488		// had a read-only tool set while the wire carried nothing. A model told to
 489		// look at the project with no way to do it invents the syntax: MiMo emitted
 490		// <bash>ls -la</bash> as prose, and one run spent 759 lines guessing at
 491		// markup. RunAside builds its own request and is deliberately not affected.
 492		if defs := c.toolDefs(); len(defs) > 0 {
 493			req.Tools = defs
 494			req.ToolChoice = "auto"
 495		}
 496		return req
 497	}

 499	// CheckRestoredContext warns if what a session *starts* with already overruns
 500	// the declared window.
 501	//
 502	// Restored context is invisible until the first request, and by then the request
 503	// has failed. aider #2979 is the shape: an 80k-token restored history fails on
 504	// the wire, and configuring the side model for summarization does not help,
 505	// because compaction runs at the end of a turn and there has not been one yet.
 506	// Strument restores less — pins, notes, and the read-only block rather than a
 507	// conversation — but the same trap is available, and a user who pinned a large
 508	// spec last session should hear about it before typing rather than after.
 509	//
 510	// It warns rather than asking. A confirmation before the user has typed
 511	// anything is a toll on every start, and there is nothing to decide yet: the
 512	// remedy is /drop or /notes drop, which they can reach either way.
 513	func (c *Coder) CheckRestoredContext() {
 514		if c.Model == nil || c.Model.Context <= 0 {
 515			return
 516		}
 517		n := c.countMessages(c.formatMessages().allMessages()) + c.countTools()
 518		if n < c.Model.Context {
 519			return
 520		}
 521		c.Out.Warningf("This session starts with about %d tokens of context, which already reaches "+
 522			"the %d-token limit for %s.", n, c.Model.Context, c.Model.QualifiedSlug())
 523		c.Out.Printf("Use /drop to unpin files, /notes drop to discard the session notes, or /tokens to see the split.")
 524	}

 526	// checkTokens warns when the estimate reaches the input window and asks to
 527	// proceed.
 528	func (c *Coder) checkTokens(messages []llm.Message) bool {
 529		maxInput := c.Model.Context
 530		if maxInput <= 0 {
 531			return true
 532		}
 533		// The schemas count: they go out with this request like everything else,
 534		// and leaving them out made the guard cheerful about a prompt 1.3k tokens
 535		// closer to the limit than it reported.
 536		inputTokens := c.countMessages(messages) + c.countTools()
 537		if inputTokens < maxInput {
 538			return true
 539		}
 540		c.Out.Errorf("Your estimated chat context of %d tokens exceeds the %d token limit for %s!",
 541			inputTokens, maxInput, c.Model.QualifiedSlug())
 542		c.Out.Printf("To reduce the chat context:")
 543		c.Out.Printf("- Use /drop to remove unneeded files from the chat")
 544		c.Out.Printf("- Use /clear to clear the chat history")
 545		c.Out.Printf("- Break your code into smaller files")
 546		c.Out.Printf("It's probably safe to try and send the request, most providers won't charge if the context limit is exceeded.")
 547		res := c.Confirm.Confirm(ConfirmRequest{Prompt: "Try to proceed anyway?", Grant: GrantContext})
 548		return res.Yes
 549	}

 551	// moveBackCurMessages rotates cur into done on edited turns.
 552	//
 553	// aider appended a synthetic "I applied and committed your changes" user turn
 554	// here, plus an "Ok." from the assistant, because with SEARCH/REPLACE there was
 555	// no other channel: a text edit format has nothing to answer the model with.
 556	// The tool loop has one. Every edit call already gets a tool result saying what
 557	// it did to which file, so the pair would only repeat it — two fabricated
 558	// messages per turn, in a loop whose whole correction was to stop inventing
 559	// turns the model never took. The commit is reported to the user instead, where
 560	// the hash is worth something.
 561	func (c *Coder) moveBackCurMessages() {
 562		c.doneMessages = append(c.doneMessages, c.curMessages...)
 563		c.curMessages = nil
 564		c.recordedMessages = 0
 565		c.maybeSummarize()
 566	}

 568	// endTurnHistory settles the finished turn and compacts if it has outgrown the
 569	// budget. Called once from runOne's defer, after the commit and the snapshot.
 570	//
 571	// It used to be gated on `editFormat == "tool" && len(turnEditedFiles) > 0`, so
 572	// only a turn that changed a file produced any settled history at all. A live
 573	// pass found what that costs: a session of questions, or any stretch of /ask,
 574	// kept everything in curMessages — which goes on the wire in full and which
 575	// maybeSummarize never examines — so the history budget existed and nothing was
 576	// ever measured against it.
 577	//
 578	// The gate is a vestige. In aider the rotation carried a synthetic "I applied
 579	// and committed your changes" pair, which only made sense after an edit;
 580	// moveBackCurMessages's own comment records removing the pair, and the gate
 581	// stayed behind. What genuinely must not happen is rotating *mid-loop*, where
 582	// compaction would eat the tool results the next send reacts to — and that is
 583	// enforced by this running in the turn-end defer, not by asking what the turn
 584	// did.
 585	//
 586	// Rotation does not move anything on the wire: done and cur are adjacent and
 587	// both sit after the read-only block, so the split is bookkeeping. What changes
 588	// is that compaction can now see the conversation.
 589	func (c *Coder) endTurnHistory() {
 590		if len(c.curMessages) == 0 {
 591			return
 592		}
 593		c.moveBackCurMessages()
 594	}

 597	// derived from the main model's window, with a 2048 floor for small windows.
 598	// It is increased from aider's context/16.

 600		return max(context/8, 2048)

 603	// countSummaryMessages reports how many retained history messages are compaction summaries.
 604	func countSummaryMessages(msgs []llm.Message) int {
 605		n := 0
 606		for _, m := range msgs {
 607			if isSummaryMessage(m) {
 608				n++
 609			}
 610		}

 614	func validCompaction(msgs []llm.Message, beforeTokens, beforeMessages, afterTokens int) bool {
 615		return len(msgs) < beforeMessages && afterTokens < beforeTokens && hasSummaryContent(msgs)
 616	}

 618	func hasSummaryContent(msgs []llm.Message) bool {
 619		for _, m := range msgs {
 620			if isSummaryMessage(m) && strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(m.Text(), summaryPrefix)) != "" {
 621				return true
 622			}
 623		}
 624		return false
 625	}

 627	// budget. It runs only when a summarizer is wired and the model's window is
 628	// known (Context > 0) — mirroring checkTokens, which treats an unknown window
 629	// as "no limit to enforce". Synchronous: the side-model call happens here,
 630	// before the next prompt is assembled. On failure the history is left intact.
 631	func (c *Coder) maybeSummarize() {
 632		if c.Summarizer == nil || c.Model.Context <= 0 {
 633			return
 634		}
 635		budget := maxChatHistoryTokens(c.Model.Context)
 636		if !c.Summarizer.tooBig(c.doneMessages, budget) {
 637			return
 638		}
 639		if c.summaryBackoff {
 640			c.summaryBackoff = false
 641			return
 642		}
 643		c.Out.Printf("Summarizing chat history to fit the context window...")
 644		beforeTokens := c.Summarizer.total(c.doneMessages)
 645		beforeMessages := len(c.doneMessages)
 646		out, err := c.Summarizer.summarize(c.doneMessages, budget)
 647		if err != nil {
 648			c.summaryBackoff = true
 649			c.Out.Warningf("Could not summarize chat history: %v", err)
 650			return
 651		}
 652		afterTokens := c.Summarizer.total(out)
 653		if !validCompaction(out, beforeTokens, beforeMessages, afterTokens) {
 654			c.summaryBackoff = true
 655			c.Out.Warningf("Could not summarize chat history: the result was not smaller than the original history")
 656			return
 657		}
 658		c.doneMessages = out
 659		c.Out.Printf("Chat history compacted: %d tokens/%s -> %d tokens/%s; %s retained.",
 660			beforeTokens, plural(beforeMessages, "message", "messages"),
 661			afterTokens, plural(len(out), "message", "messages"),
 662			plural(countSummaryMessages(out), "summary", "summaries"))
 663	}

 665	// finalizeUsage resolves cost — (1) in-band cost, (2) config
 666	// pricing, (3) tokens only, never a fabricated $0 — merges into session
 667	// totals, and emits the immutable report. Idempotent; also deferred so a
 668	// mid-send panic can't lose accounting.
 669	func (c *Coder) finalizeUsage(u *sendUsage) {
 670		if u.finalized {
 671			return
 672		}
 673		u.finalized = true
 674	
 675		// prompt_tokens is the whole prompt. Both cache figures live under
 676		// prompt_tokens_details and are a *breakdown* of it, not additions to it:
 677		// on a cold request with a breakpoint, OpenRouter returns
 678		// prompt_tokens=14021, cache_write_tokens=14018, and
 679		// total_tokens=14026 = prompt + completion. Adding the write on top counted
 680		// most of the prompt twice, and only on models that write a cache — which
 681		// is why GPT-5.6 Luna looked like it was sending an order of magnitude more
 682		// than Haiku for the same work. Cache reads were already treated as the
 683		// subset they are; the two are the same kind of number.
 684		sent := u.prompt
 685		received := u.completion
 686		estimated := false
 687	
 688		// A request the provider refused outright — a bad key, a model slug that
 689		// does not exist, an account out of credit — was not processed: no usage,
 690		// no reply, nothing billed. Estimating it printed
 691		//
 692		//	Tokens: 735 sent, 0 received. (estimated)
 693		//
 694		// under a 401, which reads as a charge for the failure. Returning before
 695		// the counters means messageSends stays 0 and flushTurnUsage says nothing
 696		// at all, which is the honest report.
 697		//
 698		// A stream that produced text before it broke is a different case: those
 699		// tokens were generated and will be billed, so it still estimates below.
 700		if u.rejected && sent == 0 && received == 0 && !u.costKnown && c.streamedText() == "" {
 701			return
 702		}
 703

400	// runAskUser asks each of the call's questions in order through the Asker and
401	// formats the result text both sides of the exchange can read back: the
402	// question and the answer together, so the transcript stays self-describing.
403	//
404	// A validation failure is the model's mistake and reflects like any other
405	// malformed tool argument. A nil Asker is not the model's fault — it is script
406	// mode with no terminal — so that answer spends no reflection budget: the
407	// model is told to proceed on its best judgment, and the turn continues.
408	func (c *Coder) runAskUser(tc llm.ToolCall, needsReflection *bool) string {
409		a, msg := parseAskArgs(tc)
410		if msg != "" {
411			*needsReflection = true
412			return msg
413		}
414		if c.Asker == nil {
415			return "ask_user_question is unavailable without an interactive terminal; " +
416				"proceed using your best judgment and state the assumption you made"
417		}

419		var b strings.Builder
420		b.WriteString("The user answered:")
421		for _, q := range a.Questions {
422			labels := c.Asker.Ask(AskRequest(q))
423			answer := strings.Join(labels, ", ")
424			if answer == "" {
425				answer = "(no answer)"
426			}
427			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n- %q → %q", q.Question, answer)
428			c.Out.Toolf("‹answer› %s", answer)
429		}
430		return b.String()
431	}

504	// applyToolCalls dispatches the captured tool calls of a "tool"-format turn.
505	// Every call gets a tool result message appended to curMessages so the wire
506	// protocol stays well-formed on the next send. Edits apply directly (like a
507	// SEARCH/REPLACE block); suggest_command and request_files are proposals the
508	// user confirms. A call the model can fix — a search that didn't match, a
509	// malformed argument — records its error as the tool result and the turn
510	// re-sends (reflection) without a synthetic user turn.
511	func (c *Coder) applyToolCalls(ctx context.Context) SendOutcome {
512		if len(c.partialToolCalls) == 0 {
513			return OutcomeSuccess
514		}
515	
516		var edits []plannedEdit
517		var commands []toolCommand
518		var commit *commitArgs
519		results := map[string]string{} // call id -> result text
520		needsReflection := false
521	
522		// Read-only calls answer immediately, in the order the model made them.
523		// Edits are collected first and applied as one batch below, so sequential
524		// edits to one file compose and the whole batch commits together.
525		for _, tc := range c.partialToolCalls {
526			switch tc.Name {
527			case toolEdit, toolWrite:
528				e, msg := parseEditArgs(tc)
529				if msg != "" {
530					results[tc.ID] = msg
531					needsReflection = true
532					continue
533				}
534				edits = append(edits, e)
535			case toolBash:
536				cmd, msg := parseCommandArgs(tc)
537				if msg != "" {
538					results[tc.ID] = msg
539					needsReflection = true
540					continue
541				}
542				commands = append(commands, cmd)
543			case toolCommit:
544				ca, msg := parseCommitArgs(tc)
545				if msg != "" {
546					results[tc.ID] = msg
547					needsReflection = true
548					continue
549				}
550				if commit != nil {
551					// One per step. Edits in a message apply as one atomic batch —
552					// that is what makes sequential edits to a file compose — so a
553					// second commit here has nothing of its own to close. Two
554					// commits are two steps, which the loop already gives for free
555					// once these results re-send.
556					results[tc.ID] = "One commit per step. This call closed nothing: " +
557						"make the next chunk of edits, then commit that."
558					needsReflection = true
559					continue
560				}
561				parsed := ca
562				commit = &parsed
563			case toolRead:
564				results[tc.ID] = c.runRead(tc)
565			case toolGrep:
566				results[tc.ID] = c.runGrep(tc)
567			case toolGlob:
568				results[tc.ID] = c.runGlob(tc)
569			case toolLS:
570				results[tc.ID] = c.runLS(tc)
571			case toolSymbol:
572				results[tc.ID] = c.runSymbol(tc)
573			case toolCheck:
574				results[tc.ID] = c.runCheckTool(ctx, tc)
575			case toolWebfetch:
576				f, msg := parseFetchArgs(tc)
577				if msg != "" {
578					results[tc.ID] = msg
579					needsReflection = true
580					continue
581				}
582				results[tc.ID] = c.runWebfetch(ctx, f)
583			case toolWebsearch:
584				q, msg := parseSearchArgs(tc)
585				if msg != "" {
586					results[tc.ID] = msg
587					needsReflection = true
588					continue
589				}
590				results[tc.ID] = c.runWebsearch(ctx, q)
591			case toolSkill:
592				s, msg := parseSkillArgs(tc)
593				if msg != "" {
594					results[tc.ID] = msg
595					needsReflection = true
596					continue
597				}
598				results[tc.ID] = c.runSkill(ctx, s)
599			case toolCode:
600				cc, msg := parseCodeArgs(tc)
601				if msg != "" {
602					results[tc.ID] = msg
603					needsReflection = true
604					continue
605				}
606				results[tc.ID] = c.runCode(ctx, cc)
607			case toolAskUser:
608				// Not routed through confirmGrouped: a question is not a permission
609				// prompt, and --yes must not answer it.
610				results[tc.ID] = c.runAskUser(tc, &needsReflection)
611			default:
612				results[tc.ID] = fmt.Sprintf("Unknown tool %q.", tc.Name)
613			}
614		}
615	
616		// Edits apply directly. The commit comes at turn end, once, so a result
617		// here names what the call did rather than a commit that has not happened.
618		edited := c.applyToolEdits(edits, results, &needsReflection)
619		for _, f := range edited {
620			c.turnEditedFiles[f] = true
621			if !c.DryRun {
622				// Nothing landed under --dry-run, so there is nothing for the
623				// automatic checks to check.
624				c.editedSinceCheck = true
625			}
626		}
627	
628		// Shell commands run after the edits, so a test run in the same turn sees
629		// the edited files.
630		for _, cmd := range commands {
631			if ctx.Err() != nil {
632				// Stopped before this one started. Running it anyway would fail
633				// instantly against the cancelled context and read, to the model,
634				// as the command itself failing.
635				results[cmd.callID] = "Not run: the user stopped the turn before this command started."
636				continue
637			}
638			results[cmd.callID] = c.runShellTool(ctx, cmd)
639		}
640	
641		// The commit closes the work, so it runs after both the edits and the
642		// commands: "commit what I did" includes the test that proved it. A model
643		// that wants to gate a commit on a result has to see that result first,
644		// which is a second step by construction.
645		if commit != nil {
646			results[commit.callID] = c.runCommitTool(*commit)
647		}
648	
649		// Append one tool result per call, in call order, then re-send on them.
650		c.appendToolResults(results)
651	
652		// Either way the next send re-enters on the tool results already appended
653		// to curMessages, adding no user turn. The two outcomes differ only in
654		// which budget they spend: a failure the model must fix is a reflection, a
655		// result it merely needs to see is a work step.
656		c.resumeInPlace = true
657	
658		// A Ctrl-C that landed while a tool was running is an interrupt, and has
659		// to be reported as one.
660		//
661		// sendMessage decides "interrupted" from how the *stream* ended, and tool
662		// calls run after the stream. So a Ctrl-C during a command used to kill
663		// the command and return OutcomeContinue: the turn carried on, the steer
664		// menu never appeared, and a second press inside the chord window quit
665		// Strument outright. None of the three is what the user asked for by
666		// pressing it.
667		//
668		// The tool results are already appended, so the history stays well-formed
669		// — every call has an answer, which is what an interrupt during *streaming*
670		// cannot promise and why that path drops partial calls instead.
671		if ctx.Err() != nil {
672			c.noteToolInterrupt()
673			return OutcomeInterrupted
674		}
675	
676		if needsReflection {
677			return OutcomeReflect
678		}
679		return OutcomeContinue
680	}

703	// runShellTool confirms and runs a shell command, returning its output as the
704	// tool result. The output always returns to the model (it answers the tool
705	// call); there is no separate add-to-chat step.
706	func (c *Coder) runShellTool(ctx context.Context, cmd toolCommand) string {
707		if !c.SuggestShellCommands {
708			return "Shell commands are disabled in this session; the command was not run."
709		}
710		// Refused here rather than in runAndShow, which is where the same check
711		// also lives for the paths that do not come through this tool. Leaving it
712		// only there meant the user was asked to approve a command that was then
713		// refused regardless — a prompt whose answer changes nothing, which is the
714		// precise way to teach someone that prompts are noise.
715		if c.Sandbox.blocksExecution() {
716			return c.Sandbox.refusal()
717		}
718		command := strings.TrimSpace(cmd.command)
719	
720		// A command that *is* one of the project's configured checks runs without
721		// asking. The user wrote it in their own config, so the prompt would be
722		// asking them to re-approve their own decision — and a prompt that fires on
723		// every `go test ./...` is what teaches them to answer without reading.
724		//
725		// It runs through runChecks rather than the shell: the parse proved the
726		// command equals the configured argv, so executing that argv directly is the
727		// only version where what ran is certainly what was compared. Sending the
728		// model's string back through a shell would reopen word splitting and
729		// globbing between the check and the execution.
730		if name, ok := matchConfiguredCheck(command, c.Check); ok {
731			// The purpose is deliberately not printed. It exists to inform a
732			// decision, and here there is no decision; what the user needs is which
733			// check matched and how it went, which runChecks' own two lines say.
734			transcript, _ := c.runChecks(ctx, []string{name})
735			// %q rather than quoteToolArg, which drops the quotes on a word that
736			// does not need them: this sentence is showing the model a call it can
737			// copy, and check(test) is not one.
738			return fmt.Sprintf("That command is the configured check %q, so it ran without asking the "+
739				"user. Call check(%q) to run it directly.\n\n%s", name, name, transcript)
740		}
741	
742		// "a = all this turn" is offered only when the sandbox is enforcing, and the
743		// condition is the whole argument rather than a detail of it.
744		//
745		// Without one, a blanket turn-scoped yes is the last thing this gate should
746		// offer: what reaches it is the open-ended remainder left over once every
747		// observation tool has taken its share, and approving the next unseen
748		// command because the last one was fine is exactly the reflex the prompt
749		// exists to interrupt. That argument is about *consequences*, though, not
750		// about the reflex — and a sandbox is precisely a bound on consequences. A
751		// command approved unseen can no longer write outside the project, so the
752		// worst case stops being unbounded and starts being "a wasted turn and a
753		// /undo".
754		//
755		// Tying the affordance to the property that licenses it also puts the
756		// incentive the right way round: the way to be asked less is to turn the
757		// sandbox on, not to reach for --yes-shell.
758		group := ""
759		if c.Sandbox.Active {
760			group = "shell"
761		}
762		if !c.confirmGrouped(ConfirmRequest{
763			Prompt:  "Run shell command?",
764			Command: command,
765			Purpose: cmd.purpose,
766			Group:   group,
767			Grant:   GrantBash,
768		}) {
769			return "The user chose not to run the command."
770		}
771	
772		exitCode, output := c.runAndShow(ctx, command)
773		return fmt.Sprintf("Command: %s\nExit status: %d\nOutput:\n%s", quoteToolArg(command), exitCode, output)
774	}

788	// applyToolEdits applies edit-tool calls in order against a shared overlay so
789	// sequential edits to one file compose, records each call's result text into
790	// results, and returns the edited relative paths. A search that doesn't match
791	// sets *matchFailure and records a focused error (with a did-you-mean) for
792	// that call.
793	func (c *Coder) applyToolEdits(edits []plannedEdit, results map[string]string, matchFailure *bool) []string {
794		if len(edits) == 0 {
795			return nil
796		}
797	
798		fen := editblock.Fence{Open: c.fence.open, Close: c.fence.close}
799		reader := diskReader{root: c.Root}
800		pending := map[string]string{}
801		needDirtyCommit := map[string]bool{}
802		writeVerb := map[string]string{} // path -> "Created"/"Overwrote"/"Applied edit to"
803		callVerb := map[string]string{}  // call id -> the same, for that one call
804		applied := map[string]bool{}     // call ids whose edit made it into the batch
805		orig := map[string]string{}      // path -> contents before the batch's first write
806		lastCall := map[string]string{}  // path -> the call that produced its final contents
807		var writeOrder []string
808		editedSet := map[string]bool{}
809		var edited []string
810	
811		read := func(path string) (string, bool) {
812			if content, ok := pending[path]; ok {
813				return content, true
814			}
815			return reader.ReadFile(path)
816		}
817	
818		for _, e := range edits {
819			// Fold an absolute spelling away before anything keys on it. unsafePath
820			// below has already accepted exactly these, so this is a rename of the
821			// bookkeeping, not a second gate.
822			e.path = c.normalizeToolPath(e.path)
823			if reason := c.unsafePath(e.path); reason != "" {
824				c.Out.Errorf("Skipping edit to %s: %s", quoteToolArg(e.path), reason)
825				results[e.callID] = fmt.Sprintf("Skipped %s: %s", quoteToolArg(e.path), reason)
826				continue
827			}
828			if ok, why := c.allowedToEdit(e.path, needDirtyCommit); !ok {
829				results[e.callID] = fmt.Sprintf("Skipped %s: %s", quoteToolArg(e.path), why)
830				continue
831			}
832	
833			content, exists := read(e.path)
834			var newContent string
835			if e.create {
836				// write puts down the whole file: create it fresh, or overwrite an
837				// existing one — never the old append-on-empty-search behavior.
838				newContent = e.replace
839				if exists {
840					// Say "overwrote" rather than "created", so the model does not
841					// assume the old contents survived somewhere.
842					callVerb[e.callID] = "Overwrote"
843					writeVerb[e.path] = "Overwrote"
844				} else {
845					callVerb[e.callID] = "Created"
846					if writeVerb[e.path] == "" {
847						writeVerb[e.path] = "Created"
848					}
849				}
850			} else {
851				// Ambiguity is a failure, not a coin flip.
852				//
853				// DoReplace takes the first occurrence and reports success, so an
854				// old_string appearing twice edited whichever came first and told
855				// the model "Applied the edit to x". That is precisely the failure
856				// mode edit-tool-bench criticises in *fuzzy* editing — a harness
857				// returning success on an underconstrained transformation, leaving
858				// the model reasoning from a false local success — and exact
859				// matching alone does not prevent it. Exact is not unique.
860				//
861				// The tool's own description already asks for "enough surrounding
862				// lines to match the intended location uniquely", so this enforces
863				// the contract it states rather than inventing one. The ambiguity
864				// message below was written for this case and was, until now,
865				// reachable only by accident.
866				var ok bool
867				ambiguous := editblock.CountOccurrences(content, e.search) > 1
868				if !ambiguous {
869					newContent, ok = editblock.DoReplace(e.path, content, exists, e.search, e.replace, fen)
870				}
871				if ambiguous || !ok || newContent == "" {
872					results[e.callID] = toolMatchFailure(e, content, fen)
873					*matchFailure = true
874					// The model is told through the tool result, and will usually
875					// re-read and try again. The user has to be told separately, or
876					// the diff that just scrolled past is the last word on an edit
877					// that never happened — every other outcome here prints a line,
878					// and only this one was silent.
879					if n := editblock.CountOccurrences(content, e.search); n > 1 {
880						c.Out.Warningf("Could not edit %s: the text to replace appears %d times.", e.path, n)
881					} else {
882						c.Out.Warningf("Could not edit %s: the text to replace was not found.", e.path)
883					}
884					continue
885				}
886				callVerb[e.callID] = "Applied the edit to"
887				if writeVerb[e.path] == "" {
888					writeVerb[e.path] = "Applied edit to"
889				}
890			}
891	
892			if _, seen := pending[e.path]; !seen {
893				writeOrder = append(writeOrder, e.path)
894				orig[e.path] = content // before *this batch*, not before this edit
895			}
896			pending[e.path] = newContent
897			lastCall[e.path] = e.callID
898			if !editedSet[e.path] {
899				editedSet[e.path] = true
900				edited = append(edited, e.path)
901			}
902			applied[e.callID] = true
903			results[e.callID] = fmt.Sprintf("%s %s.", callVerb[e.callID], quoteToolArg(e.path))
904		}
905	
906		c.dirtyCommit(needDirtyCommit)
907	
908		if len(edited) == 0 {
909			return nil
910		}
911		if !c.DryRun {
912			if err := c.writeAtomically(writePlan{Writes: pending, WriteOrder: writeOrder}); err != nil {
913				c.Out.Errorf("Exception while updating files:")
914				c.Out.Errorf("%s", err.Error())
915				// The batch rolled back, so every intended write must be reported as
916				// failed or the model will assume success. It is told what happened
917				// but this is deliberately not a reflection: a filesystem failure —
918				// a full disk, a path whose parent is a regular file — is not
919				// something the model can fix by rewriting its edit, so spending the
920				// error-reflection budget on a retry that will fail identically
921				// helps nobody. The loop continues and the model decides.
922				for _, e := range edits {

 368	// DisplayPath is how the UI and the prompt name one file, from a path given
 369	// either root-relative or absolute.
 370	//
 371	// Root-relative inside the project. Root-relative one level up too — a file
 372	// beside the project directory, or one inside a sibling of it — because
 373	// ../spec.md and ../sibling-repo/include/api.h say something an absolute path
 374	// does not: that the file sits next to the work. Absolute beyond that.
 375	//
 376	// The relative-inside, absolute-outside half is not a new rule; toProjectPaths
 377	// has written the resume file that way all along, on the grounds that a
 378	// reference reached outside the project has no project-relative form worth
 379	// keeping. The one-level exception is display's own, and storage deliberately
 380	// does not take it: a stored ../sibling breaks the moment the project moves,
 381	// while a name on screen only has to be right now. Two jobs, two rules, and the
 382	// divergence is in a file nobody reads.

 385	// /usr/include/foo.h from a project three levels down read as
 386	// ../../../usr/include/foo.h — correct, and reading as though the file were
 387	// part of the project when the whole point of /read-only is that it is not.
 388	//

 390	// model call the file the same thing. That works because Workspace.contain
 391	// admits an absolute path for a pinned file, the same exemption unsafePath

 397	// displayName is DisplayPath for a caller that already holds a resolved
 398	// absolute path, skipping the re-resolve. Everything that names a pinned file
 399	// goes through one of the two.
 400	func (c *Coder) displayName(abs string) string {
 401		rel := c.relFname(abs)
 402		up, rest := 0, rel
 403		for {
 404			if rest == ".." {
 405				up++
 406				rest = ""
 407				break
 408			}
 409			if !strings.HasPrefix(rest, "../") {
 410				break
 411			}
 412			up++
 413			rest = rest[len("../"):]
 414		}
 415		// rest == "" is the project's parent directory itself, which is not a file
 416		// anyone pins; it falls through to the absolute form rather than being
 417		// named "..".
 418		if up == 0 || (up == 1 && rest != "") {
 419			return rel
 420		}
 421		// Native separators, not ToSlash. A root-relative name is the tool-facing
 422		// form — read, grep, and ls all report forward slashes, and it has to match
 423		// them. An absolute name is not in that world: it is a path outside the
 424		// project, which the user will read, copy, and paste somewhere else, so it
 425		// should look the way their OS spells one. CI caught the difference as
 426		// C:/Users/... where Windows means C:\Users\...
 427		return filepath.Clean(abs)
 428	}

 481	// c.Confirm.Confirm directly.
 482	//
 483	// Both maps are read on every call regardless of scope. A group is only ever
 484	// written to one of them, so this cannot widen a grant; what it does is keep a
 485	// session grant honored by a request that forgot to set GroupSession.
 486	func (c *Coder) confirmGrouped(req ConfirmRequest) bool {

 494			} else {
 495				c.turnAutoApprove[req.Group] = true

 497		}

 510	// runOne is the turn loop. It keeps sending while the model has something to
 511	// react to — a tool result it hasn't seen (OutcomeContinue) or a mistake to fix
 512	// (OutcomeReflect) — and stops when the model has nothing left to say, the
 513	// human interrupts, or a budget is spent. The turn boundary is still the
 514	// human's: nothing here starts new work of its own.
 515	func (c *Coder) runOne(ctx context.Context, userMessage string) {
 516		c.initBeforeMessage()
 517		c.turnHistory = ""
 518	
 519		if userMessage == "" {
 520			return
 521		}
 522		message := userMessage
 523	
 524		// Committing and rotating settled history are both turn-end concerns.
 525		// Mid-loop the tool results must stay in cur, and summarizing them away
 526		// between steps would compact the very results the next send reacts to;
 527		// committing mid-loop would spend one commit per send on fragments of one
 528		// change. A defer covers every exit — budget declined, reflection cap,
 529		// interrupted, or done. An interrupted turn's edits are real, so they are
 530		// committed too.
 531		defer func() {
 532			c.settleEdits("")
 533			c.endTurnHistory()
 534			// Last, so the accounting closes the turn: the commit line above it, and
 535			// nothing under it. This is what the per-send reorder was reaching for,
 536			// now at the scope where a reader actually wants the number. Once per
 537			// turn even when the turn was steered, because a steered turn is still
 538			// one turn's spend.
 539			c.flushTurnUsage()
 540		}()
 541	
 542		// Outcome-driven so a re-send that carries no message text — both a tool
 543		// reflection and a tool continuation re-enter on the appended tool results
 544		// — keeps the loop going.
 545		for {
 546			outcome, reflection := c.sendSteerable(ctx, message)
 547			// After the send, not during it: sendMessage does its interrupt
 548			// handling before returning, and that handling can retract messages.
 549			c.recordNewMessages()
 550			c.lastSendOutcome = outcome
 551	
 552			switch outcome {
 553			case OutcomeReflect:
 554				if c.numReflections >= c.MaxErrorReflections {
 555					c.Out.Warningf("Only %d reflections allowed, stopping.", c.MaxErrorReflections)
 556					return
 557				}
 558				c.numReflections++
 559				message = reflection
 560	
 561			case OutcomeContinue:
 562				c.numSteps++
 563				if c.numSteps >= c.MaxSteps && !c.confirmMoreSteps() {
 564					return
 565				}
 566				message = "" // the tool results are the message
 567	
 568			case OutcomeSuccess:
 569				// The model has nothing more to call, so it believes it is done.
 570				// That is the moment to check, if the project asked us to.
 571				report, ok := c.runAutoCheck(ctx)
 572				if !ok {
 573					return
 574				}
 575				message = report
 576	
 577			case OutcomeInterrupted:
 578				next, keepGoing := c.afterInterrupt()
 579				if !keepGoing {
 580					return
 581				}
 582				c.accumulateInterrupt(next)
 583				message = next
 584	
 585			case OutcomeLooping:
 586				next, keepGoing := c.afterLoop()
 587				if !keepGoing {
 588					return
 589				}
 590				c.accumulateInterrupt(next)
 591				message = next
 592	
 593			default:
 594				return
 595			}
 596		}
 597	}

 599	// accumulateInterrupt saves the content of a send that was stopped before the
 600	// next send resets it, so the transcript can show the full arc of a steered
 601	// turn: what the model was saying, the steer, and the final answer.
 602	//
 603	// The steer is included when the user typed a custom correction rather than
 604	// choosing "Continue" (which carries no user text). A blockquote prefix makes
 605	// the authorship unambiguous in the markdown transcript.
 606	func (c *Coder) accumulateInterrupt(steer string) {
 607		if c.partialResponseContent != "" {
 608			c.turnHistory += c.partialResponseContent + "\n\n"
 609		}
 610		if steer != "" {
 611			c.turnHistory += "> " + strings.ReplaceAll(steer, "\n", "\n> ") + "\n\n"
 612		}
 613	}

 615	// sendSteerable runs one send under a context of its own, so that stopping the
 616	// send does not have to mean ending the turn.
 617	//
 618	// This is the whole of the change that makes steering possible. Ctrl-C used to
 619	// cancel the *turn's* context: everything downstream saw Canceled from then on,
 620	// and there was no way back into the loop even though the conversation itself
 621	// had survived intact. A child context per send moves the blast radius to the
 622	// one send, and the turn context stays live to make the next one.
 623	//
 624	// The tool calls of a send run inside it too — applyToolCalls takes this same
 625	// context — so Ctrl-C still kills a bash command that is running, which is the
 626	// property worth not losing.
 627	func (c *Coder) sendSteerable(ctx context.Context, message string) (SendOutcome, string) {
 628		sctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 629		c.sendMu.Lock()
 630		c.cancelSend = cancel
 631		c.sendMu.Unlock()
 632	
 633		defer func() {
 634			c.sendMu.Lock()
 635			c.cancelSend = nil
 636			c.sendMu.Unlock()
 637			cancel()
 638		}()
 639	
 640		return c.sendMessage(sctx, message)
 641	}

 643	// InterruptSend stops the send in flight without ending the turn.
 644	//
 645	// Called from the REPL's signal handler, which used to cancel the turn context
 646	// directly. A Ctrl-C between sends finds no send to cancel and does nothing,
 647	// which is correct: there is nothing in flight, and the prompt the user is
 648	// about to get asked is the interrupt they wanted.
 649	func (c *Coder) InterruptSend() {
 650		c.sendMu.Lock()
 651		cancel := c.cancelSend
 652		c.sendMu.Unlock()
 653		if cancel != nil {
 654			cancel()
 655		}
 656	}

 658	// settleEdits commits the turn's edits so far and records a snapshot to undo
 659	// them by.
 660	//
 661	// Factored out of the turn-end defer because an interruption is also a place
 662	// this belongs. The human stopped to look at something, which makes that point
 663	// a review boundary: `git show` gives exactly what the model did before it was
 664	// stopped, separately from what it did after the correction, and /undo steps
 665	// through the two halves one at a time. Anyone who wanted one commit has
 666	// /squash.
 667	//
 668	// What is *not* here is flushTurnUsage. The spend is a property of the turn,
 669	// not of each leg of it, so it stays in the defer and reports once.
 670	func (c *Coder) settleEdits(message string) {
 671		// Nothing written since the last settle, so there is nothing to settle.
 672		// Without this an interrupted-then-steered turn settles twice over the same
 673		// edits: the second commit finds the tree already matching HEAD and
 674		// announces "the turn left the files as they were", which is true of the
 675		// second attempt and false of the turn.
 676		//
 677		// turnSnap is the right signal rather than turnEditedFiles, which
 678		// accumulates across the whole turn because the history record at turn end
 679		// wants every file the turn touched. turnSnap is emptied by
 680		// pushTurnSnapshot and rebuilt by recordWrites, so it means precisely
 681		// "written since the last settle".
 682		if c.turnSnap.empty() {
 683			return
 684		}
 685		c.commitTurn(message)
 686		c.pushTurnSnapshot()
 687	}

 689	// afterInterrupt asks the human what a stopped turn should do next, and
 690	// reports the message to resume with and whether to resume at all.
 691	//
 692	// The choice is put through the Asker port, which is what ask_user_question
 693	// already uses to prompt in the middle of a turn — so this is a shape the
 694	// terminal handling has been driving all along rather than a new one. Free text
 695	// comes back as the raw line, which *is* the correction, so there is nothing to
 696	// parse. A nil Asker means no interactive terminal (script mode): stopping is
 697	// the only honest answer there, and it is what an interrupt has always done.
 698	//
 699	// The --yes flags deliberately do not answer this. They skip permission
 700	// prompts, and being asked what you meant by stopping is not a permission
 701	// prompt — the same line the port's own documentation draws for
 702	// ask_user_question.
 703	func (c *Coder) afterInterrupt() (message string, keepGoing bool) {
 704		if c.Asker == nil {
 705			return "", false
 706		}
 707		// The edits so far belong to the interrupt, whichever way this goes.
 708		c.settleEdits("")
 709	
 710		answer := c.Asker.Ask(AskRequest{
 711			Question: "You stopped the model. What now?",
 712			Options: []AskOption{
 713				{Label: "Continue", Description: "Carry on from where it was cut off"},
 714				{Label: "Stop", Description: "End the turn here"},
 715			},
 716		})
 717		if len(answer) == 0 {
 718			return "", false
 719		}
 720		switch answer[0] {
 721		case "Continue":
 722			// Say what the user decided, or the model is answering the wrong
 723			// question.
 724			//
 725			// noteInterrupt runs before this prompt, so all it can say is that the
 726			// reply was cut off. On its own that reads as a full stop, and the
 727			// model obliges: "No problem — I'll stop here. What would you like me
 728			// to do next?" It is not misreading anything. Asked afterwards what it
 729			// had been told, it quoted the cut-off note and said no continue choice
 730			// had reached it, which was exactly right.
 731			//
 732			// The rest of the wording closes the other failure mode. With a whole
 733			// partial reply above it and no instruction about what to do with it, a
 734			// model will also quite reasonably begin again from the top — which is
 735			// what an earlier live pass showed, and what was wrongly written up as
 736			// the cost of keeping the partial rather than as this bug.
 737			c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(
 738				"The user chose to continue. Pick up exactly where your reply above "+
 739					"stops and carry on from there — do not start over, do not repeat "+
 740					"or summarize what you already wrote, and do not ask what to do next."))
 741			// The notes are the message, so the next send re-enters on them rather
 742			// than appending an empty user turn to carry nothing.
 743			c.resumeInPlace = true
 744			return "", true
 745		case "Stop":
 746			return "", false
 747		default:
 748			// Anything else the user typed is the steer, and it goes in as their
 749			// own words in their own voice. They really did type it.
 750			return answer[0], true
 751		}
 752	}

 754	// afterLoop asks what to do about a reply the harness stopped for repeating
 755	// itself, and reports whether the turn should continue.
 756	//
 757	// Its own function rather than a branch of afterInterrupt, because both halves
 758	// differ. The question cannot say "you stopped the model" — the user did not —
 759	// and "Continue" cannot mean "pick up exactly where your reply stops", which
 760	// here is an instruction to resume the loop. What is offered instead is a
 761	// retry: the loop's note (send.go) tells the model to take a different
 762	// approach, and the most useful thing the user can do is type what that should
 763	// be, which the free-text steer already carries.
 764	func (c *Coder) afterLoop() (message string, keepGoing bool) {
 765		if c.Asker == nil {
 766			return "", false
 767		}
 768		// The edits so far belong to the stopped reply, whichever way this goes.
 769		c.settleEdits("")
 770	
 771		answer := c.Asker.Ask(AskRequest{
 772			Question: "The model was repeating itself and was stopped. What now?",
 773			Options: []AskOption{
 774				{Label: "Stop", Description: "End the turn here"},
 775				{Label: "Try again", Description: "Let it answer again, told not to repeat itself"},
 776			},
 777		})
 778		if len(answer) == 0 {
 779			return "", false
 780		}
 781		switch answer[0] {
 782		case "Stop":
 783			return "", false
 784		case "Try again":
 785			// The note noteLoop already appended is the whole message: it says what
 786			// was stopped and what to do instead, so the next send re-enters on it
 787			// rather than appending an empty user turn to carry nothing.
 788			c.resumeInPlace = true
 789			return "", true
 790		default:
 791			// Anything else the user typed is the steer, in their own voice.
 792			return answer[0], true
 793		}
 794	}

 796	// runAutoCheck runs the project's check_auto checks at the end of a turn that
 797	// edited files, and reports whether the turn should continue.
 798	//
 799	// It fires here rather than after each edit because a mid-turn state is
 800	// legitimately broken: edit one file, then its caller, and in between nothing
 801	// compiles. Checking there would spend budget on failures the model was already
 802	// about to fix. At turn end the model has declared itself finished, which is
 803	// exactly when an independent check is worth something — and the reason to make
 804	// it independent is that the model's judgement about *which* check mattered is
 805	// the part that fails. A run that passed the tests and never linted still
 806	// reports "the checks pass".
